sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Two separate figures carry the name Lot. The first is an Irish woman warrior of the unearthly Fomorians. She led her folk in the war against the people of Partholón. The tales show her as plain, with long lips on her breasts and four eyes on her back. The second Lot is a minor figure of Arthurian legend. He wed the half sister of King Arthur, named Morgause. He was the father of Gawain, a knight of the Round Table. He fell to the powerful king Pellinore during the fight for the throne. The sons of the two kings then kept a lasting feud.

okr.objective: Separate the two figures who share the name Lot.
key_results: One Lot is an Irish woman warrior of the Fomorians.
She is described as plain with lips on her breasts and four eyes on her back.
The Arthurian Lot marries the half sister of Arthur.
His sons keep a feud after his fall to Pellinore.
